newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends off as interbank rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends off as interbank rates fall.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed marginally off at 484.50/485.50 per dollar as interbank lending rates softened to between five and 24 percent from Friday's five to 75 percent range, traders said.
The bolivar closed Friday at 484.00/485.00 per dollar.

"Most of the trade was on the interbank market, there was hardly any corporate demand," said one trader adding that many investors still feared the bolivar may be entering a faster rate of depreciation.
"There was a lot of speculative trade," said another broker.
Venezuela continues to pursue an inflation-fighting strong bolivar policy, where the currency ostensibly floats between slowly depreciating bands set by Central Bank intervention.
Critics say the policy has left the bolivar increasingly over-valued with the exchange rate little-changed since price and currency controls were removed in April last year.
Increasing fears of over-valuation have recently heightened exchange rate volatilty.
